title: Dario Amodei clears the air on banning open-weight AI models
excerpt: Amodei said he never advocated for banning open-weight AI models and doesn't believe a ban to be effective in making AI safer.
content_html:
Dario Amodei rejects speculations that Anthropic wants to ban all open-weight AI models

By Katherine Li

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Dario Amodei is clearing the air on open-weight AI models.

The Anthropic CEO on Monday pushed back against claims that his AI startup wants Washington to ban open-weight AI models and said that critics have misunderstood the company's position.

"Anyone who has read my past writing should know that I don't regard such bans as a useful measure, but let me state it clearly so that there is no doubt: Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models," Amodei wrote in his blog post.

"Open-weights models that don't have dangerous capabilities are a public good," Amodei added.

Rather than banning open models, Amodei said in his blog post that policymakers should focus on preventing advanced AI chips from reaching authoritarian governments, cracking down on industrial-scale AI "distillation" used to copy frontier models

The clarification comes after a Senate proposal sparked fears that Washington could move to restrict open-weight AI models. In response, Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Google, OpenAI, and dozens of other companies signed a letter urging lawmakers not to pursue broad limits, with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang emerging as one of the industry's most outspoken advocates for open-weight AI.

Anthropic declined to sign, fueling speculation that it wants to ban open-weight models to protect its business.

Amodei's post also sharpened one of the biggest fault lines in the AI industry's debate over open-weight models. While he agreed the industry should increase competition and give customers greater control, he rejected the argument that making model weights public inherently makes AI safer.

"I don't agree with the letter's assertions that open-weights models necessarily make it easier to develop safeguards or that broad access to capabilities necessarily helps defenders more than attackers," he wrote, adding that capable models could quickly weaponize pandemic-level viruses, but developing defense could take years.

"It seems at least as likely to me that the opposite will be true," Amodei added.

Dario Amodei 否认 Anthropic 希望禁止所有开放权重 AI 模型的猜测

作者：Katherine Li 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

Dario Amodei 正在为开放权重人工智能模型扫清障碍。

这位 Anthropic 首席执行官周一反驳了有关他的人工智能初创公司希望华盛顿禁止开放权重人工智能模型的说法，并表示批评者误解了该公司的立场。

“任何读过我过去的文章的人都应该知道，我并不认为此类禁令是一种有用的措施，但让我清楚地说明这一点，以便毫无疑问：Anthropic 从未主张禁止开放权重模型，”Amodei 在他的博客文章中写道。

“不具有危险功能的开放权重模型是一种公共物品，”阿莫迪补充道。

阿莫迪在博客文章中表示，政策制定者不应禁止开放模型，而应重点关注防止先进人工智能芯片进入独裁政府，打击用于复制前沿模型的工业规模人工智能“蒸馏”

这一澄清是在参议院的一项提案引发人们担心华盛顿可能采取行动限制开放权重人工智能模型之后作出的。 作为回应，英伟达、微软、Meta、谷歌、OpenAI 和其他数十家公司签署了一封信，敦促立法者不要追求广泛的限制，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋成为业界最直言不讳的开放式人工智能倡导者之一。

Anthropic 拒绝签署，这引发了人们对其希望禁止开放重量模型以保护其业务的猜测。

阿莫代的帖子还加剧了人工智能行业关于开放权重模型争论中最大的断层之一。 虽然他同意行业应该增加竞争并给予客户更大的控制权，但他拒绝接受模型权重公开本质上会使人工智能更安全的论点。

他写道：“我不同意这封信的主张，即开放权重模型必然使开发防护措施变得更容易，或者广泛获得能力必然对防御者比攻击者有更多帮助。”他补充说，有能力的模型可以快速武器化大流行级别的病毒，但开发防御可能需要数年时间。

阿莫代补充道：“至少在我看来，情况恰恰相反。”
